turns.doctor_question: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?
turns.patient_response: Hi. Thanks. Well, what finally made me come in is that I just keep making these small, but really embarrassing mistakes. Like, I'll turn in applications or research notes, and I'll find out later that I mislabeled an artwork date or completely skipped a question. And the thing is... I honestly thought I had checked them over before submitting them. It's just getting pretty frustrating.

symptom_reasoning.S001: The patient explicitly reports making small, embarrassing mistakes such as mislabeling dates or skipping questions on applications and research notes despite thinking they had checked them.

turns.doctor_question: Do you often have trouble staying focused on a task, even when you want to pay attention?
turns.patient_response: I don't think so, no. When I sit down to work on something, I feel like I'm paying attention. I don't really notice myself zoning out or losing focus when I'm trying to get a task done. It's more just... making those small mistakes I mentioned, even though I feel like I'm focused on it the whole time.

symptom_reasoning.S001: The patient mentions making small mistakes despite feeling focused, indicating detail inattention errors.
symptom_reasoning.S002: The patient explicitly denies having trouble staying focused or zoning out when trying to get a task done.

turns.doctor_question: Do you find yourself repeatedly checking your work over and over, even after you already know you’ve looked at it?
turns.patient_response: No, not really. I usually just look it over once, maybe twice, and think it's fine. I don't sit there checking it over and over again. I just... I assume I caught everything when I looked at it the first time, so I submit it and move on. It's only later that I realize I missed something.

symptom_reasoning.S001: The patient notes that they often realize later they missed something, indicating careless mistakes or a failure to give close attention to details.
symptom_reasoning.S066: The patient explicitly denies repeatedly checking their work over and over, ruling out checking compulsions.

turns.doctor_question: Do you often feel worried or on edge, even when there isn’t one specific problem causing it?
turns.patient_response: No, not really. I mean, I get frustrated when I realize I messed up on an application or something, but I don't just feel worried out of nowhere. I'm usually pretty relaxed unless there's an actual reason to be stressed out.

symptom_reasoning.S056: The patient explicitly denies feeling worried out of nowhere, stating they only get stressed for actual reasons.
symptom_reasoning.S058: The patient denies feeling on edge, stating they are usually pretty relaxed.

turns.doctor_question: Do you often start tasks but have trouble finishing them?
turns.patient_response: No, not really. If I sit down and start something, I usually finish it. I mean, I might make those careless mistakes along the way, like I mentioned, but getting to the end isn't really the issue. I don't usually leave things half-done. Once I start a task, I just push through until I submit it.

symptom_reasoning.S001: The patient explicitly mentions making careless mistakes along the way.
symptom_reasoning.S004: The patient denies leaving things half-done and states they usually finish tasks once started.

turns.doctor_question: Are you easily distracted by things going on around you while you're working?
turns.patient_response: Yeah, definitely. If I'm sitting at my desk trying to read or write, almost anything can pull my focus. Like, if a siren goes by outside, or I hear someone talking out in the hallway... I just lose my place. Even just a random thought, like an idea for an exhibit or something, will pop into my head, and I'll get completely sidetracked. Sometimes twenty minutes will go by before I even realize I stopped working.

symptom_reasoning.S008: The patient explicitly confirms being easily distracted by extraneous stimuli (sirens, people talking) and unrelated thoughts (ideas for an exhibit) while trying to work.

turns.doctor_question: Looking back, were you already this easily distracted as a child?
turns.patient_response: Yeah, I think so. Even back in elementary school, my teachers would write notes saying that I had good ideas, but I'd always forget to turn in my worksheets or I'd somehow lose the instructions. I was always missing little details like that. Honestly, nothing really got turned in unless my parents checked my backpack every single night to make sure I had everything.

symptom_reasoning.S001: The patient explicitly states they were 'always missing little details' in their schoolwork.
symptom_reasoning.S004: The patient mentions they would 'always forget to turn in my worksheets,' indicating a failure to follow through on schoolwork.
symptom_reasoning.S007: The patient notes they would 'somehow lose the instructions' needed for their tasks.
symptom_reasoning.S008: The patient confirms the doctor's question about being easily distracted as a child by saying 'Yeah, I think so.'
